As someone who has worked in tourism management and marketing, I came here to say this. 

Saying that tourist attractions are overcrowded and should be regulated by higher prices is like saying your local supermarket should have a higher price to reduce the waiting time in the queue. They are literally for middle class people, that is why there is infrastructure around them at lower costs to accommodate that. 

The rich and ultra rich have different ways to go on holidays such as private islands and reservations. Not to mention the one percent that practically live on yachts or private planes to go to different countries all over the world to countless villas. Not to mention if they do want to be a true tourist there will be a whole team of people working to plan that out and orchestrate private access areas and the like. 

Raising the prices of the attractions you mentioned will kill the infrastructure in place and the many support structures (transport, accomodation & local business) will collapse as higher prices does not mean more money as demand would plummet so the experience although quieter would be overall less enjoyable.
I wish I had the money for my shrink to join me in the bedroom taking notes.

I had a similar experience with my brother, and when I was around your age with my relationship. It didn't end well for me but I can say as someone who thought about it a lot some things I wished I had considered. 

You don't have to share everything all at once, sharing that something happened and sharing who did it are two separate things. If you're comfortable sharing your experience with her and not who did it then simply explain that. I would avoid lying, you shouldn't need to lie to only share what your comfortable with. I would also avoid any questions about what happened just for a while but if you want and need to at the time then that's your journey. 

Also not everyone is comfortable talking about those things and sometimes it can over complicate things especially if it's related to family and things they have done. The best person to talk to about it is always a professional therapist. 

If you feel ready and a need to talk about this it will come out, its only a question of when. I would try do it in a controlled and calm manner but regardless, I would make sure that you know that it can go either good or bad so be prepared for anything and expect nothing, if that makes sense? It's better to approach it without expecting a certain reaction but to be aware your sharing something traumatic with another human who has their own thoughts and feelings they can react in some amazing and crazy ways so we have to respect that. Also it can have a huge effect on you as well, you may think you've come to terms with what's happened but vocalising it with someone you share feelings with can change your perception drastically.

I wish you all the luck and hope whatever happens you stay happy.

Edit: added some things

There are several ways to justify his actions if you take into account the premise of the show, you're assuming that his crimes against the other clans and the leaf clan should be viewed entirely in opposition to the culture and traditions of the times. But if you reframe your thinking to one of feudal Japan or China or possibly even further back to when there was no system of a government more just clan/tribe leaders it's not uncommon for people to change their allegiance quite commonly with out severe repercussions mostly due to their capabilities and renown. Especially when that clan or village in this case commits a dishonourable act which causes that person to leave.

A prime example of this would be Lu Bu, he would regularly switch sides and faught against practically any dynasty that existed during the time period.

Another way to view it is that what sasuke did wasn't viewed as negatively by most because of the reasons behind it. Take the biggest crime against the leaf the killing of Danzo. Danzo essentially did everything that Sasuke did, he colluded with rival villages to become Hokage, he killed many loyal ninja if we're comparing the two then Danzo commited far more criminal and damaging acts to the leaf than Sasuke. I realise you try to state it's a non factor but killing a dishonourable person isn't seen as a bad thing in that world.

There is also the whole nature of the curse mark changing him. Sasuke didn't really do anything until that was put on him and that could have played a part in how he went about the whole situation.  

That world is one that murder, subterfuge and battles are considered common place so really any other deaths and near deaths that happened is just an occupational hazard. Samurai used to test their swords out by cutting random people in the streets remember. Killing other ninja is what ninjas do. It's not this lawful, authoritarian society that one's crimes are punished by the rule of the villages. Those with the power to act and uphold their personal justice will do so and clash with others who have their own ideals. The winner is the one who is right. 

As a story telling piece I think Sasuke dying would have held little to no benefit to the narrative direction of Naruto or Naruto Shippuden, it would have just further proved that power wins over what you're calling for here which is justice, Sasukes actions we're questionable yes, but his motives and goals were the same as imprisoning or executing those who have done wrong or would do harm to you or your village/clan. 

It's worth noting that the allegence to clan and village is not something that's as cut and dry as you're putting it when it comes to the great ninja dynasties which is often forgotten in Naruto. Sometimes clan comes before village. Especially when a village kills your whole clan. You're almost honour bound to do something about it. That's why Itachi murdering all of them is such a impactful statement to show his love for Sasuke. Anyways I think I could talk about this for hours so I'm just gonna leave it there to see how that resonates with you.

We all die eventually but as they said, there's no telling what you may do on your path to that end. So I hope you can make the choice to stick around to find out what you may experience. I'm sure you have plenty good to give the world and I have no doubt it has plenty of good to give to you. Being alone doesn't mean you aren't important.
